title: Known by Your Light
core_idea: Some traditions imagine a spirit world where souls are seen by their light rather than their mistakes; even as an image, it can invite us to look at ourselves and others more kindly now.
text: Some traditions describe the spirit world in a surprising way. Not as a courtroom where every mistake is read aloud, but as a place where each soul is recognized by its light. The kindness it carried. The love it tried to give, even clumsily. Whether or not that world exists exactly as imagined, the image itself can be a gentle teacher. Most of us remember our own failures in sharp detail, while our quiet goodness fades into the background. Perhaps you could try seeing yourself the way those traditions picture it, just for tonight. Not ignoring what went wrong, but noticing the light that was there all along. And maybe offering that same view to someone else.
description: A reflection on one image of the spirit world, where souls are known by their light, and what it might teach us about kindness now.
